svg.title: Cybersecurity From Zero: a beginner roadmap
svg.desc: A cyberpunk-styled beginner guide to starting cybersecurity: ground rules, the CIA triad, an 8-step roadmap, a 30-day starter plan, a starter toolkit and common career paths.

g.text: Practice only in your own VMs
Take notes on everything you do
only the right people can read data
systems work when people need them
stack controls, never trust just one
How computers, operating systems and the internet work: IP, DNS,
HTTP/HTTPS and ports. Everything in security builds on this.
Files, permissions, processes, pipes, grep and ssh. Run Ubuntu or
Kali in a virtual machine and get comfortable in the terminal.
IP addressing, subnets, the TCP handshake, DNS and firewalls.
Watch real traffic in Wireshark; use ping, traceroute and curl.
PRACTICE ▸ Capture and read your own traffic
Start with Python, then Bash. Automate small jobs: a port checker,
a log parser, a file hasher. Pick up C and JavaScript later.
PRACTICE ▸ Build one small tool every week
CIA triad, authentication, hashing vs encryption, phishing, SQL
injection, XSS, malware. Read OWASP Top 10 and MITRE ATT&CK.
VirtualBox or VMware, a Kali VM and targets made to be broken
(DVWA, Juice Shop) on an isolated host-only network.
PRACTICE ▸ Snapshot it, break it, restore it
CTF games and guided labs teach faster than reading. Start easy,
read other people's write-ups, then redo them yourself.
PRACTICE ▸ picoCTF / TryHackMe / Hack The Box
Choose SOC, pentesting, AppSec, forensics or GRC. Certs help but
are optional; write-ups and projects prove real skill.
PRACTICE ▸ CompTIA Security+ is a common first cert
ONE HOUR A DAY IS ENOUGH
▸ Learn cd, ls, cat, chmod, grep
▸ Study IP, DNS, HTTP and ports
▸ Break DVWA or Juice Shop in lab
▸ Join a CTF team or Discord
WARNING: ONLY TEST SYSTEMS YOU OWN OR HAVE WRITTEN PERMISSION TO TEST.
DOES ▸ Monitor alerts, investigate and respond
DOES ▸ Test systems with permission, report findings
DOES ▸ Find and fix flaws in web and mobile apps
Read write-ups, then rebuild them yourself.
Ask questions and share what you learn.
For education only. Stay legal, stay ethical,
and never test systems without permission.
